summary: the cases of tests/run gnu on x86-64, against faults in the kernel, in the password driver, in the ntpd row's configuration and in the SNTP server

argv: ARCH=x86_64 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 build/tests/system/ptydrive && ARCH=x86_64 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel && cp build/tests/system/ptydrive tests/system/gnu_rows.sh tests/system/sntpserver.py ${WORK}/
ARCH=x86_64 exec sh tests/proofs/guest.sh run gnu

faults.name: kernel-and-driver
faults.summary: execve names the new image by the path it was given in place of the path its walk took; the console's descriptors 0, 1 and 2 get split modes and the console answers POLLOUT on a writable descriptor alone, so that tmux at a console login draws nothing; and ptydrive sends the password without its last byte

edits.find:
want = (short)(want | (events & POLLOUT));
        return tty_poll(&console_tty, want, wq);

faults.name: no-server
faults.summary: the row writes /etc/ntp.conf with its server line commented out, so init starts no ntpd, the clock is never set, and the row waits until its step's bound

lines: run: gnu: machine.gnu.ntpd on x86_64: failure:
row failed: ssh: the step's bound expired

faults.name: host-time
faults.summary: the SNTP server serves the host's own time in place of the time that began in 2030, so ntpd keeps the clock near the host's

lines: run: gnu: machine.gnu.ntpd on x86_64: failure:
